previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, chronic abdominal pain, anxiety, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had elevated white blood cell count and hyperglycemia on admission. Her pain was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and her home tramadol. A femoral central line was placed due to poor IV access but was removed during the stay due to infection risk. She experienced one episode of hypoglycemia from taking mealtime insulin without eating, which resolved with treatment. Urine culture grew multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, but without signs of active infection, it was not treated. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up on pending blood cultures and to adjust insulin use when not eating.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ is a ___ y/o F with PMHx of IDDM, GERD, HTN, depression, 
recurrent UTI's, chronic abdominal pain with extensive negative 
work-up ultimately attributed to anxiety, gastroparesis, and 
GERD who presented with urinary frequency and different 
abdominal pain from her typical abdominal pain syndrome, 
diagnosed with complicated UTI. Now s/p PICC line and treating 
with zosyn x 10 days.  
 
 24/hr/Overnight Events/Subjective: She states her abdominal 
pain is still there but I observed her eat a large, cheesy 
sausage, egg, and cheese sandwich without any issues while I was 
speaking with her this morning. No other complaints. Denies 
diarrhea, last BM was yesterday. 

Rest of her hospital course/plan are outlined below by issue: 

#complicated klebsiella UTI: per OMR note, pt was given 
fosfomycin x 1 by the ED for UTI prior to admission. Last UCX 
with ecoli and klebsiella. Pt reported continued urinary 
frequency and different abdominal/flank pain than what was 
consistent with
her chronic abdominal pain syndrome. 
-s/p PICC placement, IV zosyn for complicated UTI course likely 
for 10 days, last day ___

#diarrhea with h.o C.diff-started empiric flagyl given apparent 
vancomycin allergy. Cdiff was negative so was discontinued. 
Intermittent diarrhea likely relates to her ongoing antibiotic 
therapy. 

#chronic Abdominal pain: Despite prior workup. Felt to be 
related to gastroparesis, GERD, anxiety. In the ED the patient 
was given lorazepam, ketorolac for pain  and had a femoral line 
placed for IV access (unable to place  peripheral IV). 
-continue Zofran, tramadol, lyrica, lidocaine patch, tylenol

# Diabetes-type 2: Her blood glucose was elevated on admission.
-DM diet, continue home regimen of lantus (35units per pt) and 
Humalog with HISS.

# Leukocytosis/thrombocytosis. Her leukocytosis/thrombocytosis 
was thought to be an acute flare of her chronic hematologic  
abnormalities related to a stress response and due to her UTI. 

==============
CHRONIC ISSUES
==============
# Anxiety. For her anxiety- continue  home clonazepam,
risperidone, and propranolol. 
# Depression- continued on sertraline and risperidone. 
# GERD. Continue sucralfate and omeprazole 
# Hypertension- Continue Imdur, nifedipine, and propranolol.
